E8 - Dataset-based workload (measured runtimes)

Input sample_genome.fa parsed with Bio.SeqIO: 3/3 records valid, 1,200,000 bases, GC 46.0%. 80 tasks executed on Linux-6.18.44-fc-v114-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 (Python 3.13.16); burst = median of 3 timed runs; estimate = calibrated cost model (R² gc_content 0.99, kmer_count 0.99, motif_search 0.76, alignment 0.98; mean relative estimate error 17%). Hardware monitor during profiling: {'cpu_percent_mean': 33.4, 'cpu_percent_max': 100.0, 'mem_percent_mean': 8.3, 'samples': 80}. Single workload (no CI); timings vary slightly between runs.

E10 - Hardware validation (real execution)

60 dataset tasks really executed on 1 worker process(es) (one core left for the dispatcher) by a user-space dispatcher that uses the same policy code; 5 repetitions with rotated algorithm order. Non-preemptive policies only (Adaptive-NP = adaptive scoring without quantum). Average waiting (ms), mean [95 % CI]:

Algorithm hardware simulation (profiled bursts) simulation (replayed bursts)
FCFS 60.64 [51.94, 69.33] 54.54 [54.54, 54.54] 57.81 [49.95, 65.68]
SJF 34.92 [28.07, 41.78] 28.93 [28.93, 28.93] 33.00 [27.12, 38.88]
Priority 50.82 [34.93, 66.71] 38.36 [38.36, 38.36] 47.04 [32.44, 61.64]
Adaptive-NP 33.17 [26.86, 39.48] 29.65 [29.65, 29.65] 31.10 [26.57, 35.63]

Hardware waiting includes inter-process communication latency; replayed simulation uses the bursts measured in that hardware run, so the gap between the two is the dispatcher overhead the simulator does not model. These are user-space measurements, not an OS-kernel scheduler.

Gantt charts, event and decision logs (16 tasks, 2 cores, load 1.5)

Per-algorithm charts with idle intervals: FCFS, SJF, SRTF, RR(q=10), Priority, Adaptive. Event logs (ARRIVE, DISPATCH, PREEMPT, QUANTUM_EXPIRE, COMPLETE, IDLE_START, IDLE_END) are in gantt/*_events.csv; decision_log_adaptive.csv gives the score breakdown of every Adaptive dispatch decision; task_log_adaptive.csv the task-level log.
